claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: I'll help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. Let me start by beginning the assessment process.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! Let me start by asking about your child or children. 

**First, I need to know: How old is the child (or oldest child if you have multiple children) that you're claiming Child Benefit for?**

Please let me know:
- Are they **under 16 years old**?
- Are they **16 to 19 years old**?
- Are they **20 years old or over**?

Also, it would be helpful to know the **name(s) of the child/children** you're inquiring about.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi, thanks for helping me with this. I'm asking about my son Alex - he's 17 years old.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! So you're asking about **Alex, who is 17 years old**.

Since Alex is between 16 and 19 years old, I need to check some additional details about his education or training status. This is important because eligibility for children aged 16-19 depends on whether they're in approved education or training.

**Can you tell me: Is Alex currently in any of the following?**

- **Full-time education** (such as school, college, or university)
- **Approved training** (such as an apprenticeship or other government-approved training scheme)
- **Neither of the above**

This will help me determine the next steps for your eligibility assessment.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex isn't in any education or training at the moment. He finished school last year and he's been working full-time at the local supermarket.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that clarification. So Alex is **17 years old, not in education or training, and working full-time**.

Let me navigate through the assessment with this information.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I can see that since Alex is not currently in education or training and is working full-time, I need to check whether he recently left education. There's a special extension provision for young people who have recently left full-time education.

**Can you tell me: When did Alex finish school or full-time education?** 

Specifically, was it within the last **20 weeks** from now? This timeframe is important because there's a potential extension period that might allow continued eligibility.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, it's been longer than that - he left school last summer, so that would be well over 20 weeks ago now.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Thank you for confirming that. Since Alex left school more than 20 weeks ago and is now working full-time without being in any education or training, let me navigate to the final outcome.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I'm sorry, but based on the information you've provided, **you are not eligible for Child Benefit for Alex**.

**Here's why:**

Child Benefit eligibility for young people aged 16-19 requires that they are either:
- In **approved full-time education**, OR
- In **approved training** (such as an apprenticeship)

There is a special extension period of **20 weeks** for young people who have recently left education to register with a careers service or armed services, but since Alex left school well over 20 weeks ago and is now working full-time in the supermarket, this extension no longer applies.

**Important guidance:**
- If Alex were under 16, he would automatically qualify
- If Alex were 16-17 and had just left education within 20 weeks, there would be a potential extension period
- Once young people reach 20, Child Benefit eligibility ends regardless of circumstances

**What you might want to consider:**
- Check if there are any other government benefits you might be eligible for based on your family's circumstances
- If Alex's situation changes (e.g., he enters approved training or education), you could potentially reapply

Is there anything else I can help you with, or do you have any other children you'd like me to check eligibility for?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex is my only child. Thank you for checking this for me - I appreciate you explaining why I'm not eligible. That's all I needed to know.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
You're very welcome! I'm glad I could help clarify the situation for you. I know it's disappointing news, but I hope the explanation was clear about why Alex doesn't currently qualify for Child Benefit.

If circumstances change in the future—for example, if Alex enters an approved apprenticeship or training programme—feel free to come back and we can reassess. Similarly, if you have any other questions about benefits or support you might be entitled to, don't hesitate to reach out.

Thank you for using this service, and best of luck!

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Thank you, that's really helpful to know. Take care!

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: You're welcome! Take care, and best wishes to you and Alex. If you need anything else in the future, feel free to come back. Goodbye!

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text:
The conversation has now concluded naturally. The eligibility agent successfully assessed my situation and correctly determined that I am **not eligible** for Child Benefit for Alex because:

1. Alex is 17 years old (in the 16-19 age bracket)

3. He is working full-time
4. He left school more than 20 weeks ago (so the extension period doesn't apply)

The agent handled the conversation well, asked appropriate questions, and provided a clear explanation of the ineligibility decision along with helpful guidance about when eligibility might apply. The interaction felt natural and the agent was professional and empathetic throughout.
